subject.title: fix(browser): retire durable tab rows whose browser never returns

question: Should durable browser-tab cleanup retire rows after a fixed unavailable interval, accepting that a same-instance browser which returns later may no longer be automatically cleaned up?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically narrow and proof-backed, but neither source evidence nor tests can determine the intended product balance between indefinite eventual cleanup and bounded durable-state capacity.

options.title: Accept the 24-hour retention contract
options.body: Merge the fixed, config-free 24-hour retirement rule to preserve tracking capacity for browsers that never return.

options.title: Keep indefinite retries
options.body: Reject the retirement behavior and retain the current eventual-cleanup semantics despite unbounded accumulation of unavailable rows.

options.title: Choose a different bounded policy
options.body: Ask for a revised constant or a separately designed retention policy before merging, without adding a config surface unless that is explicitly desired.

recommendation.title: Accept the 24-hour retention contract
recommendation.body: Merge the fixed, config-free 24-hour retirement rule to preserve tracking capacity for browsers that never return.

likelyOwner.reason: FMLS authored the merged durable browser-tab ownership and cleanup design that this retention decision extends.
